questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb. The committee decided to ______ the meeting until next week due to the lack of quorum.
questions.solution: Elimination: The context 'until next week' indicates postponement. 'Put on' means to wear or stage an event; 'put up' means to accommodate or tolerate; 'put away' means to store or save. 'Put off' is the standard phrasal verb meaning 'to postpone' or 'delay', fitting the context perfectly.

questions.text: The average weight of 25 students is 50 kg. When the teacher's weight is included, the average increases by 1 kg. What is the teacher's weight?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Teacher's weight = New average + (Number of students × Increase) = 51 + 25×1 = 76 kg. Full: Total weight of 25 students = 25×50 = 1250 kg. New total for 26 persons = 26×51 = 1326 kg. Teacher = 1326 − 1250 = 76 kg.

questions.text: The average age of a family of 5 members is 28 years. If the age of the youngest member is 10 years, what was the average age of the family at the time of the birth of the youngest member?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total present age = 5 × 28 = 140 years. 10 years ago, the youngest was not born. Total age of remaining 4 members 10 years ago = 140 - 10 - (4 × 10) = 90 years. Required average = 90 / 4 = 22.5 years. Full: Sum of ages now = 140. Youngest is 10. Ten years ago, the youngest was not born, so only 4 members existed. Each of the 4 members was 10 years younger. Sum of their ages 10 years ago = (140 - 10) - 40 = 90. Average = 90 / 4 = 22.5.

questions.text: In the following question, a statement is given followed by two conclusions. Assuming the statement to be true, decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s). Statement: K ≥ L > M = N ≤ O < P Conclusions: I. K > N II. P > M

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Chain the inequality signs directly. For I: K ≥ L > M = N ⇒ K > N (True). For II: P > O ≥ N = M ⇒ P > M (True). Both follow. Full Solution: Combine the statement into a single chain: K ≥ L > M = N ≤ O < P. Check Conclusion I: The path from K to N is K ≥ L > M = N. Since '>' appears in the chain (L > M), K is definitely greater than N. Check Conclusion II: The path from P to M is P > O ≥ N = M. Since '>' appears (P > O), P is definitely greater than M. Hence, both conclusions follow.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The board decided to ______ the discussion on the merger proposal until the next quarterly meeting.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Part-of-Speech & Meaning Elimination. The structure 'to ______' requires a base form Verb. 'Deferral' (Noun) and 'Deference' (Noun) are eliminated. 'Differ' means 'disagree' (context mismatch). 'Defer' means 'postpone' (fits perfectly). Step-by-step: 1. Grammar check: 'to' + Verb (V1). Options A, B are verbs; C, D are nouns -> Eliminate C, D. 2. Meaning check: Context implies postponing. 'Defer' = Postpone. 'Differ' = Disagree. 3. Select 'Defer'.

questions.text: Choose the word that best fits the blank in the following sentence: The committee ______ the proposal after thorough deliberation, citing budget constraints.
questions.solution: The phrase "citing budget constraints" signals a negative outcome. "Approved" contradicts this, "postponed" would normally be followed by "due to" rather than "citing", and "ignored" does not align with "after thorough deliberation". Hence "rejected" is the only word that fits both grammatically and contextually.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. A alone can complete it in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Let total work = LCM(12,20)=60 units. A+B efficiency = 5 units/day, A efficiency = 3 units/day → B efficiency = 2 units/day. Work done in 4 days = 20 units, remaining = 40 units. B takes 40/2 = 20 days. Full solution: B's 1 day work = 1/12 - 1/20 = 1/30. Together 4 days work = 4/12 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. Days for B = (2/3) ÷ (1/30) = 20 days.

questions.text: Rearrange the following five sentences (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph. (1) The new digital platform allows farmers to sell their produce directly to buyers across the country. (2) This eliminates the need for middlemen who often exploit the growers. (3) Consequently, the profit margins for small-scale farmers have increased significantly. (4) The government launched the initiative last year to boost agricultural income. (5) Registration on the portal is free and requires only a valid land record document.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Opening Sentence & Mandatory Pairs. Sentence 4 introduces the topic (Government initiative) -> Best Opener. Pair (1)-(5): Platform features followed by registration process. Pair (2)-(3): 'This eliminates...' (Cause) -> 'Consequently...' (Effect). Sequence: 4-1-5-2-3. Step-by-step: 1. Identify opener: Sentence 4 (Independent intro). 2. Link 1->5 (Platform -> Registration details). 3. Link 2->3 (Demonstrative 'This' in 2 refers to 1/5; 'Consequently' in 3 follows 2). 4. Verify flow: 4 (Launch) -> 1 (Feature) -> 5 (Process) -> 2 (Benefit) -> 3 (Result).

questions.text: Given below are two sentences. Which of the given starters can combine them into a single sentence without changing the meaning? 1. The interest rates have been hiked by the RBI. 2. The EMIs for home loans are expected to rise. (i) With the interest rates having been hiked by the RBI... (ii) Since the interest rates have been hiked by the RBI... (iii) Although the interest rates have been hiked by the RBI...
questions.solution: Elimination: Starter (iii) 'Although' introduces a contrast, but the rise in EMIs is a direct consequence, not a contradiction, of the rate hike. Starter (i) uses a participle phrase ('With... hiked') correctly showing the attendant circumstance/cause. Starter (ii) uses the subordinate conjunction 'Since' correctly establishing the cause-effect relationship. Both (i) and (ii) form grammatically and logically correct complex sentences.

questions.text: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5:4. Four years ago, the ratio of their ages was 4:3. What is the present age of A?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Let ages be 5x and 4x. Four years ago: (5x−4)/(4x−4) = 4/3 ⇒ 15x−12 = 16x−16 ⇒ x = 4. A = 5x = 20 years. Full: Constant age difference = x. Four years ago ratio 4:3 gives difference = 1 part = x. So 5x−4 = 4x ⇒ x = 4. Present age of A = 5×4 = 20 years.

questions.text: Rahul starts from point X and walks 10 m North. He turns right and walks 15 m. Then he turns left and walks 10 m. Finally, he turns right and walks 5 m to reach point Y. What is the shortest distance between point X and point Y?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate net displacement along North-South and East-West axes. North displacement = 10 + 10 = 20 m. East displacement = 15 + 5 = 20 m. Shortest distance = √(20² + 20²) = √800 = 20√2 m. Full Solution: Start at origin. Move N 10 (0,10). Right (E) 15 (15,10). Left (N) 10 (15,20). Right (E) 5 (20,20). Distance from (0,0) to (20,20) = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m.

questions.text: What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following expression? (You are not expected to calculate the exact value) √1024 × 12.98 + (15.02)² - ? = (256 ÷ 8) × 7.99

In a row of students facing North, A is 15th from the left end and B is 20th from the right end. If there are exactly 6 students sitting between A and B, and A is to the left of B, what is the total number of students in the row?
questions.solution: Shortcut: When A is left of B with 'n' persons between, Total = Rank(A from Left) + Rank(B from Right) + Persons Between. Calculation: 15 + 20 + 6 = 41. Full Solution: Position of A from left = 15. Position of B from right = 20. Since A is left of B, the sequence is [Left... A ... (6 students) ... B ... Right]. Total students = (Students left of A including A) + (Students between) + (Students right of B including B) = 15 + 6 + 20 = 41. Overlapping case check: Sum of ranks (35) > Total (41) is false, so non-overlapping formula applies directly.

questions.text: Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils can never be Sharpeners.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply chain rules: Some + All = Some; Some + No = Some Not; All + No = No. Full: Some Pens are Pencils + All Pencils are Erasers ⇒ Some Pens are Erasers. This + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ Some Pens are not Sharpeners (I follows). All Pencils are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ No Pencil is Sharpener ⇒ All Pencils can never be Sharpeners (II follows).

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming the statements are true, decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s). Statements: 1. Some Tables are Chairs. 2. All Chairs are Beds. 3. No Bed is a Sofa. Conclusions: I. Some Tables are not Sofas. II. All Chairs can never be Sofas.

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Some + All = Some' and 'Some + No = Some Not' rules. Some Tables are Chairs + All Chairs are Beds ⇒ Some Tables are Beds. Some Tables are Beds + No Bed is Sofa ⇒ Some Tables are not Sofas (I follows). All Chairs are Beds + No Bed is Sofa ⇒ No Chair is Sofa ⇒ All Chairs can never be Sofas (II follows). Full Solution: From Statements 1 and 2: 'Some Tables are Chairs' and 'All Chairs are Beds' implies 'Some Tables are Beds'. Combining this with Statement 3 ('No Bed is a Sofa'): 'Some Tables are Beds' + 'No Bed is Sofa' ⇒ 'Some Tables are not Sofas'. Conclusion I follows. From Statements 2 and 3: 'All Chairs are Beds' + 'No Bed is Sofa' ⇒ 'No Chair is Sofa'. This means it is impossible for any Chair to be a Sofa, so 'All Chairs can never be Sofas' follows. Conclusion II follows.
